policies.title: IPv4 forwarding is enabled
policies.description: Checks that a non-router host does not forward packets.
policies.rationale: A forwarding host can be abused to bridge networks. Routers, VPN and container hosts legitimately need it, so treat a failure as a prompt to confirm intent.
policies.absence_note: The kernel default (or a distribution drop-in) applies and cannot be known from this file alone: result is unknown.
policies.remediation: Set net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0 on hosts that are not routers.
references: Linux kernel documentation: sysctl/net, sysctl/kernel, sysctl/fs (public)

policies.title: IPv4 source-routed packets are accepted
policies.description: Checks that the sender cannot dictate the packet route.
policies.rationale: Source routing lets an attacker steer traffic around filters.
policies.absence_note: The kernel default (or a distribution drop-in) applies and cannot be known from this file alone: result is unknown.
references: Linux kernel documentation: sysctl/net, sysctl/kernel, sysctl/fs (public)

policies.title: ICMP redirects are accepted
policies.description: Checks that ICMP redirects cannot change the routing table.
policies.rationale: Forged redirects can reroute traffic through an attacker.
policies.absence_note: The kernel default (or a distribution drop-in) applies and cannot be known from this file alone: result is unknown.
references: Linux kernel documentation: sysctl/net, sysctl/kernel, sysctl/fs (public)

policies.title: ICMP redirects are sent
policies.description: Checks that a non-router does not send ICMP redirects.
policies.rationale: Hosts that are not routers have no reason to advertise better routes.
policies.absence_note: The kernel default (or a distribution drop-in) applies and cannot be known from this file alone: result is unknown.

policies.title: Reverse-path filtering is off
policies.description: Checks that packets arriving on an interface that would not route back are dropped.
policies.rationale: It blunts source-address spoofing. Asymmetric routing setups may need loose mode (2).
policies.absence_note: The kernel default (or a distribution drop-in) applies and cannot be known from this file alone: result is unknown.
references: Linux kernel documentation: sysctl/net, sysctl/kernel, sysctl/fs (public)

policies.title: ICMP echo to broadcast addresses is answered
policies.description: Checks that the host ignores broadcast pings.

policies.title: TCP SYN cookies are disabled
policies.description: Checks that SYN cookies protect the listen queue under flood.
policies.rationale: Without them a SYN flood can exhaust the backlog.

policies.title: Packets with impossible addresses are not logged
policies.description: Checks that spoofed or misrouted addresses are logged.
policies.rationale: The log gives defenders evidence of spoofing or routing mistakes.

policies.title: Address space layout randomisation is not full
policies.description: Checks that stack, heap and mappings are randomised.
policies.rationale: ASLR makes memory-corruption exploits less reliable.

policies.title: Kernel pointers are exposed to users
policies.description: Checks that kernel addresses are hidden from unprivileged users.
policies.rationale: Leaked addresses help defeat ASLR in kernel exploits.

policies.title: Kernel log is readable by all users
policies.description: Checks that only privileged users can read the kernel ring buffer.

policies.title: Any process may ptrace its peers
policies.description: Checks that the Yama ptrace restriction is on.

policies.description: Checks that link-following races in shared directories are blocked.

policies.description: Checks that unprivileged users cannot load BPF programs.

policies.title: IPv6 router advertisements are accepted
policies.description: Checks that a static-addressed host ignores router advertisements.
policies.rationale: Rogue advertisements can redirect IPv6 traffic. Hosts that rely on SLAAC need them.
policies.absence_note: The kernel default (or a distribution drop-in) applies and cannot be known from this file alone: result is unknown.
policies.remediation: Set net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_ra = 0 where addressing is static.
references: Linux kernel documentation: sysctl/net, sysctl/kernel, sysctl/fs (public)
